ideas.what: Port Corwin's RE-AIM stage (experiments/ext_corwin-biocel-aux/ker11_reaim_plugin_v24.py, apply_reaim(csv_in, csv_out)) as a new fail-soft LAST stage of the K2/K3 build: `--patch reaim`, env BIOHUB_REAIM_ENABLE default 0 (then the file is byte-identical), gate 7.0 um, margin 2.0 um, per-run wall budget (e.g. 20 min total, then pass-through). Input is K2's final submission.csv. For every track end (a node with no child before the last frame) it takes the t+1 nodes within 7 um of p + flow(p), INCLUDING nodes that already have a parent, puts their current parents into a local Hungarian on flow-compensated distance, and applies the local solution only if the total cost drops by more than 2 um. It never adds, moves or deletes a node, never gives a source a second child, keeps every existing fork (all asserted in the code), and writes the input unchanged with 'REAIM_DISARMED' on any exception. It needs only numpy and polars, both already in x138's environment.
ideas.why_now: This is the only new mechanism in today's intel that needs no training, keeps the node set and is scale-free. x138 already has a flow-prior motion relink (DIFF.md: FLOW_MODE seed, K 12, R 40) and sister symmetry 0.6, so Corwin's flow relink is NOT new, but a post-canon track-end re-solve that can take a target away from its current parent is not in x138. Our closed lines were relink THRESHOLDS inside x138's own relink and the ILP-trusting stitch/edge filter. RE-AIM uses geometry only and runs after linefit, readmit and gapfill. Its author is a 0.965 team (#17) that built it as a plug-in on its 'v31' world. It is GT-free, and only 2 constants (7 um and 2 um) were chosen on train, so an exp60 lab arm is close to out-of-sample, unlike the edge-net lab that fooled us before (+0.016 local vs 0 LB). It is also very cheap: CPU seconds per clip against about 4 h of unused hidden-run headroom.
ideas.evidence: corwin1979/biocel-aux-4d9e2c17 (public CC0 dataset, 19 Sep, 287 downloads; https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/corwin1979/biocel-aux-4d9e2c17), pulled to experiments/ext_corwin-biocel-aux/ (NOTES.md). The file's docstring states the contract; I quote only its fail-soft marker, 'REAIM_DISARMED'. Corwin is public LB #17 at 0.965 (CLI LB 25 Sep 16:52 UTC). x138 already has the flow relink: experiments/ext_x138/DIFF.md line 69; grep of biohub-x138.ipynb shows _flow_predictor and FLOW_MODE. No LB delta for RE-AIM is stated anywhere (the file refers to an internal 'DF_m2' measurement without a number).
ideas.expected_gain: Unknown sign; guess +0.000 to +0.002 public (central ~+0.0005). It works on the edge term only (track ends vs orphan starts). Node count term: exactly 0.
ideas.runtime_cost: Guess < 5 s per clip on CPU: local Hungarians only at track ends, and the flow field is a KD-tree median; Corwin timed a similar flow field at 1.8 s per 30k nodes. With a hard total cap of 20 min that is <= 0.35 h against ~4 h headroom.
ideas.test_gate: (1) Dummy gate: node rows identical to K2 (sha256 of node rows), 'REAIM_ARMED' line present, no source with more than one child, fork count >= K2's, and DISARMED forced by a bad path gives a CSV byte-identical to K2. (2) exp60 lab arm on the 28 SELECTION clips, applied to the replayed K2 tail. Pass: delta >= +0.001 on SELECTION and >= 0 on CONFIRMATION, with the node band 0. (3) LB by R4: it changes edges, so it goes into F1 only at +0.002, or else is an F2 candidate. Must be decided before R8 (27 Sep 12:00 UTC), so it runs as an extra arm of the 26 Sep exp60 lab and needs no new GPU slot.
ideas.effort_hours: 3-4 (1 h builder patch plus byte-identity test, 1 h lab arm, 1 h dummy and gates)
ideas.risk: (a) x138's relink, gapfill and readmit may already have used up the recoverable track ends, making it a no-op. (b) Taking a target from its incumbent parent can break a correct link: Corwin's own notes record div_fp +3/+2 at small margins, which is why the margin is 2 um. (c) Positions after linefit may be floats; apply_reaim casts to int for the flow, so check that K2's CSV dtypes are kept by _rewrite. (d) It must stay OFF under _deadline_degraded, like the insertion gate. (e) Licence: CC0; the source must be credited in the winner write-up.

ideas.what: Optional and lower priority. Add Corwin's public pair LightGBM (pair_gbm_core15_boot.txt, 15 geometric columns from pair_features.py, loaded with a sha guard by pair_ship.py) as a SECOND additive bonus term in x138's motion_relink_edges cost: cost -= PAIR_BONUS * p_pair, with a seed pass, following pair_ship.py's four-site recipe. Env default 0 = byte-identical.
ideas.why_now: It is a learned pair prior from a 0.965 team, trained leave-one-embryo-out on 199 films. At the same coefficient, the vendor's own edge probability was -0.0001 in their test while this booster was +0.0017, so it carries information x138's relink lacks. It is an external public CC0 model, not our retraining, so R9 does not forbid it.
ideas.evidence: experiments/ext_corwin-biocel-aux/pair_ship.py docstring: OOF on 199 films, B_b16 +98 TP / -144 FP, dJ_edge +0.001687 (44b6 +0.0006 / 6bba +0.0019); LOEO +0.001702; the vendor-probability control -0.000104. The same docstring warns that its arm A 'IS NOT THE CHAMPION' (no gap-close or safe divisions) and that only a real run gives the delta.
ideas.expected_gain: Guess +0.000 to +0.0015 public on x138, because x138's readmit, gapfill and flow relink already capture part of it. It shifts relink choices and therefore readmit, so the node count moves slightly.
ideas.runtime_cost: Small: a seed pass of ~0.4 s per film plus LightGBM scoring of ~1M pairs per film, a few seconds each. Guess < 0.3 h total.
ideas.test_gate: The booster was trained on train GT, so an exp60 lab arm is IN-SAMPLE and cannot validate it. It could only be judged on the LB under R4 (+0.002 to enter F1), with a single pre-registered coefficient of 16 and no ladder. It needs the booster file (1.4 MB) attached as a dataset, lightgbm present in the Kaggle image, and a node-count identity check before readmit.
ideas.risk: High: it looks like the edge-filter lesson (in-sample learned edge prior, local gain, 0 on the LB). The dataset has a single version, but a later owner update would change the attached file, so pin the sha. It also costs an LB slot. My recommendation is not to do it unless RE-AIM is a no-op and a slot is spare on 27 Sep.
